label: Speed bands
description: Speed as a ratio to a reference unit. For source units it is the game's speed reference, named in the games registry: usually its basic rifle infantry, or a basic bot or medium mech where the game has none. Every unit of the game is compared with it, vehicles and aircraft included. For generated cards it is a Shamble Frontlines soldier. Compare the speeds each can keep up for as long as it likes: count a sprint or a boost only when nothing limits it (no meter, stamina or cooldown), for the reference and the unit alike. Use the stock unit: no upgrades, empty, at full health. Use the way it moves in a fight: flying speed for units that fight in the air, water speed for boats, land speed for the rest, amphibious and hover units included. Use plain open ground: the off-road speed where a game gives road and off-road speeds, off creep, with no other terrain bonus. A ratio exactly on an edge goes to the band nearer medium: 0.7 is slow, 1 and 1.5 are medium, 2.5 is fast. The validator computes the band from speed_raw the same way. With no usable figure, use comparisons. A source that compares the unit with a unit that has a band ("faster than the Prowler", "keeps pace with infantry") gives that unit's band, moved one band only when it says much faster or much slower. A speed word on its own ("fast", "slow moving") sets the band of the same name only where the registry's speed_reference says the game's words are read that way (Halo Wars 2); elsewhere it describes the unit among its own kind, so put it in notes. With nothing usable, judge from figures for neighbouring units or from footage, and add an uncertain entry for mobility/speed. If the judgement cannot tell which side of an edge the unit falls on, take the band nearer medium, as for a ratio exactly on an edge, and say so in that uncertain entry. Source units have no band for standing still.

terms.label: Slow
terms.description: From 0.7 up to but not including 1 times the reference.

terms.label: Medium
terms.description: From 1 up to and including 1.5 times the reference. The reference unit itself is medium.

terms.label: Fast
terms.description: Over 1.5 and up to and including 2.5 times the reference.
